quote: A reasonable inference may be drawn from the evidence that despite management's knowledge that the Pinto's fuel system could be made safe at a cost of but $4 to $8 per car, it decided to defer corrective measures to save money and enhance profits.
context: The trial court's characterization of management's decision-making, identifying enhanced profits as the outcome of choosing not to implement low-cost safety fixes.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: Institutional mentality of callous indifference to safety
original_label: Institutional mentality of callous indifference to safety
quote: Ford's institutional mentality was shown to be one of callous indifference to public safety. There was substantial evidence that Ford's conduct constituted "conscious disregard" of the probability of injury to members of the consuming public.
context: The trial court's characterization of Ford's organizational culture and decision-making orientation regarding consumer safety, based on the evidence presented.

label: Engineers with managerial authority made decision not to correct
original_label: Engineers with managerial authority made decision not to correct
quote: There was also evidence that Harold Johnson, an assistant chief engineer of research, and Mr. Max Jurosek, chief chassis engineer, were aware of the results of the crash tests and the defects in the Pinto's fuel tank system. Ford contends those two individuals did not occupy managerial positions because Mr. Copp testified that they admitted awareness of the defects but told him they were powerless to change the rear-end design of the Pinto. It may be inferred from the testimony, however, that the two engineers had approached management about redesigning the Pinto or that, being aware of management's attitude, they decided to do nothing. In either case the decision not to take corrective action was made by persons exercising managerial authority.
context: The trial court's analysis of how responsibility for non-action flowed through the hierarchy, addressing whether intermediate engineers had authority and used it.

label: Rear structure lacked reinforcing members other cars possessed
original_label: Rear structure lacked reinforcing members other cars possessed
quote: The Pinto's rear structure also lacked reinforcing members known as "hat sections" (two longitudinal side members) and horizontal cross-members running between them such as were found in cars of larger unitized construction and in all automobiles produced by Ford's overseas operations. The absence of the reinforcing members rendered the Pinto less crush resistant than other vehicles. Finally, the differential housing selected for the Pinto had an exposed flange and a line of exposed bolt heads. These protrusions were sufficient to puncture a gas tank driven forward against the differential upon rear impact.
context: The trial court identifies multiple structural design defects in the Pinto, noting that comparable vehicles from Ford's own overseas operations had these protective features.

label: Pinto had weaker bumper than any other American car
original_label: Pinto had weaker bumper than any other American car
quote: In addition, the Pinto was designed so that its bumper was little more than a chrome strip, less substantial than the bumper of any other American car produced then or later.
context: The trial court describes another design deficiency in the Pinto that was documented and knowable within Ford's own comparative analysis.

label: Equipping car with reinforced design would have cost $15.30
original_label: Equipping car with reinforced design would have cost $15.30
quote: Equipping the car with a reinforced rear structure, smooth axle, improved bumper and additional crush space at a total cost of $15.30 would have made the fuel tank safe in a 34 to 38-mile-per-hour rear-end collision by a vehicle the size of the Ford Galaxie. If, in addition to the foregoing, a bladder or tank within a tank were used or if the tank were protected with a shield, it would have been safe in a 40 to 45-mile-per-hour rear impact. If the tank had been located over the rear axle, it would have been safe in a rear impact at 50 miles per hour or more.
context: Expert testimony at trial establishing the cost and feasibility of making the Pinto substantially safer through design changes Ford chose not to implement.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: When prototype failed test, standard practice was to redesign
original_label: When prototype failed test, standard practice was to redesign
quote: When a prototype failed the fuel system integrity test, the standard of care for engineers in the industry was to redesign and retest it.
context: Expert testimony describing the professional standard that should have applied to the Pinto, establishing the deviation from normal practice.

label: Copp testified management made decision knowing of test results
original_label: Copp testified management made decision knowing of test results
quote: Harley Copp, a former Ford engineer and executive in charge of the crash testing program, testified that the highest level of Ford's management made the decision to go forward with the production of the Pinto, knowing that the gas tank was vulnerable to puncture and rupture at low rear impact speeds creating a significant risk of death or injury from fire and knowing that "fixes" were feasible at nominal cost.
context: Key witness Copp, positioned to know the test results and management's awareness, testifies about what top management knew and decided.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: Crash tests demonstrated vulnerability at 20-30 mph
original_label: Crash tests demonstrated vulnerability at 20-30 mph
quote: Through the results of the crash tests Ford knew that the Pinto's fuel tank and rear structure would expose consumers to serious injury or death in a 20- to 30-mile-per-hour collision.
context: The trial court's characterization of what Ford's management knew from the test data about the real-world hazard the Pinto posed.

label: JRC reports on NOx discrepancies from 2010-2011
original_label: JRC reports on NOx discrepancies from 2010-2011
quote: Since 2010-2011, several studies, including reports published by the Commission's Joint Research Centre, showed large discrepancies in nitrogen oxides emissions of diesel cars sold on the EU market.
context: The inquiry report introduces evidence that emerged from technical research conducted early in the period under investigation.

label: Indications of discrepancies known since 2004-2005
original_label: Indications of discrepancies known since 2004-2005
quote: According to the experts and witnesses heard, there were indications from at least 2004-2005 – when the proposal for the Euro 5/6 Regulation was being prepared – that, while diesel cars respected the successive legal Euro limits for NOx emissions when tested in the laboratory during the type-approval process with the NEDC, the emissions of those vehicles in real use were in fact much higher.
context: The inquiry establishes the timeline of when evidence of the gap between lab and real-world emissions first became available to decision makers.

label: JRC findings on thermal windows and memory effects
original_label: JRC findings on thermal windows and memory effects
quote: On 30 April 2012 an internal e-mail from the JRC, with DG GROW in copy, was sent on the subject of a Euro 5a diesel passenger vehicle that was being tested by the JRC. The test results showed that the Euro 5 emission limits were only fulfilled in the temperature range between 20 and 30 °C, but were not met outside of that temperature window. The e-mail also mentions a 'memory effect' that was found to influence the engine strategy for at least 20 minutes after starting the engine at a specific temperature.
context: The inquiry documents a specific internal signal about suspect emission control behavior that arrived at the Commission in April 2012.

label: Commission official characterizes behavior as hard cycle beating
original_label: Commission official characterizes behavior as hard cycle beating
quote: The official in DG GROW who replied to the e-mail, with DG ENV and DG MOVE in copy, stated that 'this is very useful and a clear case of "hard" cycle beating'.
context: A Commission official interprets the JRC test results as evidence of deliberate manipulation to pass the test cycle, using technical language that acknowledges the anomaly.

label: JRC 2013 report discusses possible defeat strategies
original_label: JRC 2013 report discusses possible defeat strategies
quote: Nevertheless, in its 2013 report entitled 'A complementary emissions test for light-duty vehicles', the JRC mentions the possibility of 'the use of defeat strategies under normal conditions of use' and states that while the use of defeat devices is generally prohibited, the exceptions that exist leave room for interpretation and provide scope, together with the currently applied test procedure, for tailoring the emissions performance of light-duty vehicles to a narrow set of type-approval conditions.
context: The JRC research team explicitly raises the possibility of defeat device use in a published 2013 report.

label: Correspondence discusses strange emissions behaviour in 2008 and 2010
original_label: Correspondence discusses strange emissions behaviour in 2008 and 2010
quote: Other correspondence between the JRC and DG GROW, DG ENV and DG CLIMA, discussing possible 'strange' emissions behaviour in 2008 and 2010, seemingly had no follow-up either.
context: The inquiry identifies multiple instances of internal Commission correspondence flagging anomalies in emissions data across a six-year period.

label: JRC research findings routed through multiple DGs without coordination
original_label: JRC research findings routed through multiple DGs without coordination
quote: Better coordination between the different Commission services involved, including the JRC, could have been instrumental in accelerating the process of adapting the tests. Better cooperation among Directorate-Generals in the development of emissions legislation and in the monitoring of its implementation could have yielded better results on air quality and the protection of public health in the EU.
context: The inquiry's formal conclusions identify the absence of coordinated information flow across Commission departments as a structural failure.

label: RDE-LDV working group composition and participation
original_label: RDE-LDV working group composition and participation
quote: In three group meetings that took place between May and September 2016 with 43 to 47 participants, 21-23 represented car manufacturers, 9-12 other automotive industry actors, 5-7 Member States, 1-5 technical services, and 1-2 research institutes, civil society or NGOs.
context: The inquiry documents the composition of the regulatory working group responsible for developing real-world emissions tests, showing how communication channels were structured.

label: Member States participation in RDE-LDV group was sparse
original_label: Member States participation in RDE-LDV group was sparse
quote: It can be concluded from the minutes provided that, with the exception of a few Member States, such as the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Germany, France, Denmark and Spain, the vast majority did not participate in the RDE-LDV working group, despite voicing criticisms of the Commission's proposals.
context: The inquiry identifies a gap between the Member States that actively participated in the regulatory process and those that remained silent despite having concerns.

label: DG GROW and DG ENV pursue separate objectives
original_label: DG GROW and DG ENV pursue separate objectives
quote: Under the Commission's principle of collective responsibility, the portfolio of the Commissioner for Industry (and the Directorate-General for Enterprise and Industry DG ENTR/GROW) includes emission standards, while the portfolio of the Commissioner for the Environment (and the Directorate-General for the Environment DG ENV) includes air quality. The two DGs pursue separate objectives but cooperate to find workable compromises.
context: The inquiry explains the organizational structure that separated responsibilities for setting emission standards from monitoring air quality, creating a fragmented decision-making context.

label: JRC findings did not reach higher levels of Commission hierarchy
original_label: JRC findings did not reach higher levels of Commission hierarchy
quote: The Commission should have ensured that the JRC's research findings and concerns discussed among the Commission services with regard to possible illegal practices by manufacturers reached the higher levels of the hierarchy – which allegedly did not happen – so that appropriate action could be taken.
context: The inquiry concludes that warning information generated at lower organizational levels did not travel to decision makers with authority to act.

label: DG GROW director-general was not informed of April 2012 email
original_label: DG GROW director-general was not informed of April 2012 email
quote: In their hearing before the committee, the then Director and Director-General of DG GROW stated that they were not informed about this e-mail and therefore no follow-up action was taken.
context: Senior officials testify that critical technical information about suspect emission behavior did not reach them despite being within their organization.

category: Rules of the game and attention-directing incentives
label: Focus on avoiding burdens on industry after 2008 financial crisis
original_label: Focus on avoiding burdens on industry after 2008 financial crisis
quote: The excessive length of the process leading to the introduction of regulatory RDE tests cannot be sufficiently explained only by the complexity of the development of a new test procedure, the time needed for the technological development of PEMS, and the length of the decision-making and administrative processes at EU level. The delays were also due to choices of political priorities, lobby influence and constant pressure from the industry that directed the focus of the Commission and the Member States to avoiding burdens on industry in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis.
context: The inquiry identifies a dominant priority framework that made regulatory stringency a lower priority than industry accommodation following the financial crisis.

category: Rules of the game and attention-directing incentives
label: Manufacturers and authorities interpreted legislation as requiring only lab test passage
original_label: Manufacturers and authorities interpreted legislation as requiring only lab test passage
quote: In their written answers and during the hearings, Member States and car manufacturers stated that they interpreted the legislation in such a way that the NEDC test in the laboratory was the only requirement for vehicles to pass, despite the air-quality objectives of the legislation.
context: The inquiry identifies a shared cognitive frame that narrowed the scope of what the regulation required, focusing attention on lab tests rather than real-world compliance.

category: Rules of the game and attention-directing incentives
label: Type-approval authorities had fee incentives tied to manufacturers
original_label: Type-approval authorities had fee incentives tied to manufacturers
quote: The fact that type-approval authorities and technical services are usually financed in part by fees paid directly to them by the car manufacturers can give rise to conflicts of interest due to the need to maintain commercial relations.
context: The inquiry identifies a financial incentive structure that could influence what issues received attention from regulators.

category: Rules of the game and attention-directing incentives
label: Manufacturers could choose among flexible type-approval authorities
original_label: Manufacturers could choose among flexible type-approval authorities
quote: Car manufacturers are, in principle, free to address the type-approval authority and technical service with the most flexible and least stringent interpretation of the rules, as well as the lowest fees.
context: The inquiry identifies a structural incentive where manufacturers could shop for regulatory interpretations, directing their attention toward lenient authorities.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: Commission focused on developing new tests rather than enforcement
original_label: Commission focused on developing new tests rather than enforcement
quote: To address the issue of NOx discrepancies, the Commission focused on the development of a new test procedure that could ensure that the emission limits were met in real driving conditions, as provided for by Article 14(3) of the Euro 5/6 Regulation.
context: The inquiry documents what the Commission chose to prioritize in response to evidence of emissions problems, showing a focus on future testing rather than present enforcement.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: DG ENV emphasis on ensuring RDE timeline while DG ENTR resisted
original_label: DG ENV emphasis on ensuring RDE timeline while DG ENTR resisted
quote: The then Commissioner Potočnik and DG ENV focused their action on ensuring that the agreed timeline for the introduction of RDE tests was respected, while the Commission services were concerned about the car manufacturers' resistance to the introduction of PEMS testing.
context: The inquiry shows different DGs attending to different priorities: environmental officials pressed for the timeline while industrial policy officials worried about manufacturer resistance.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Discrepancies attributed only to inadequate test cycle, not defeat devices
original_label: Discrepancies attributed only to inadequate test cycle, not defeat devices
quote: Before September 2015 the discrepancies were generally attributed to the inadequacy of the NEDC laboratory test, which is not representative of real-world emissions, and to the optimisation strategies put in place by car manufacturers to pass the laboratory test by calibrating vehicles' ECTs so that their effectiveness is only ensured within the boundary conditions of the NEDC test. The discrepancies were generally not attributed to the possible use of prohibited defeat devices.
context: The inquiry identifies a cognitive frame that screened out the possibility of defeat devices as an explanation for the observed anomalies, despite historical precedent.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Defeat devices not suspected despite US precedent from 1990s
original_label: Defeat devices not suspected despite US precedent from 1990s
quote: Defeat devices were generally not considered among the possible reasons behind the discrepancies between NOx emissions from diesel cars measured in the laboratory and measured on the road, because it was believed that these discrepancies could be sufficiently explained by the fact that the NEDC laboratory test was not representative of real driving, and that manufacturers could optimise their vehicles in order to pass the test cycle while apparently complying with the letter of EU law. It was not generally suspected that they could be in actual use in any passenger car produced in the EU despite the fact that such devices were found in the US in light-duty vehicles in 1995 and in heavy-duty vehicles in 1998.
context: The inquiry documents how available historical knowledge about defeat devices was discounted or forgotten, allowing a cognitive script to exclude this possibility.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: No follow-up action on 2012 JRC email about cycle beating
original_label: No follow-up action on 2012 JRC email about cycle beating
quote: The justification for why no action was taken, due to a lack of any indication or clear evidence of the possible use of defeat devices by car manufacturers, is wrong, as indications were given in the correspondence, and thus constitutes maladministration, as evidence cannot be found unless it is sought.
context: The inquiry characterizes the non-response to the April 2012 warning as involving circular reasoning: the absence of investigation meant no evidence was found, which was then used to justify the absence of investigation.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Commission did not mandate JRC to investigate defeat device possibility
original_label: Commission did not mandate JRC to investigate defeat device possibility
quote: The Commission had no legal obligation to search for defeat devices itself, but had the legal obligation to oversee the Member States' enforcement of the ban on defeat devices. However, in spite of the awareness of, and communication between the relevant Commission services on, possible illegal practices by manufacturers contravening Regulation (EC) No 715/2007, the Commission neither undertook any further technical or legal research or investigation, either on its own or by mandating the JRC, nor requested any information or further action from the Member States to verify whether the law may have been infringed.
context: The inquiry identifies a failure to escalate the investigation despite internal awareness and communication about potential violations.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: No Member State tested for defeat devices before September 2015
original_label: No Member State tested for defeat devices before September 2015
quote: No EU or Member State authority searched for defeat devices or proved the illegal use of defeat devices before September 2015. No Member State authority or technical service performed any tests other than the NEDC in the scope of type-approval, which in itself cannot point to the use of a defeat device.
context: The inquiry documents a universal absence of investigative action despite the existence of both a legal ban on defeat devices and available test methodologies.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Type-approval authorities did not analyze software or perform additional tests
original_label: Type-approval authorities did not analyze software or perform additional tests
quote: Before Volkswagen's admissions about the ECU software, type-approval authorities did not analyse software or perform any tests that would allow them to enforce the ban on defeat devices laid down in Article 5(2) of Regulation (EC) No 715/2007, limiting themselves to approving without further consideration the results of the NEDC laboratory test conducted by technical services. Tests in addition to the standard were not considered.
context: The inquiry describes how authorities narrowed their focus to a single test procedure, despite having legal authority to conduct additional verification.

label: RDE development took 4+ years with repeated delays
original_label: RDE development took 4+ years with repeated delays
quote: The working group 'Real Driving Emissions – Light-Duty Vehicles' (RDE-LDV), reporting to the TCMV, was initiated by the then Commissioner for Enterprise and Industry Antonio Tajani in January 2011, after the JRC had presented its results about the discrepancies in NOx emissions, with the objective of developing a procedure to assess the real driving emissions of light-duty vehicles in a robust manner with a view to its regulatory implementation. The work of the RDE-LDV group led eventually to approval by the TCMV of the introduction of real driving emission testing as of 2017.
context: The inquiry documents a six-year gap between the start of RDE development in January 2011 and its adoption by the TCMV in October 2015.

label: Commission did not escalate decision to Council despite authority to do so
original_label: Commission did not escalate decision to Council despite authority to do so
quote: Despite the issue of pollutant emissions from vehicles being not only a highly sensitive and political issue, but also a subject of great concern to EU citizens, the Commission did not make any attempt to advance the decision-making process by making use of the possibility envisaged in the Regulatory Procedure with Scrutiny to bring the proposal to the level of the Council in order to increase political awareness and to exercise additional pressure on obstructing Member States.
context: The inquiry identifies a procedural option the Commission possessed but did not use to overcome Member State obstruction of the RDE development.

label: Commission did not request information on emission technology at low temperatures
original_label: Commission did not request information on emission technology at low temperatures
quote: Despite the clear indications of the possible illegal use of defeat devices, the Commission never made use of the provision under Regulation (EC) No 692/2008, which entitles it to request Member States' type-approval authorities to provide information on the functioning of emission technology at low temperatures.
context: The inquiry documents a specific investigative power available to the Commission that was never invoked despite warning signals.

label: No infringement procedures on emissions before Volkswagen case
original_label: No infringement procedures on emissions before Volkswagen case
quote: As regards motor vehicles, in the past, only one infringement procedure was launched (against Germany, on air conditioning systems), while no infringement cases were ever started concerning pollutant emissions from vehicles.
context: The inquiry documents the absence of enforcement action via infringement procedures despite persistent evidence of NOx emissions problems.

label: Member States delayed RDE adoption and blocked qualified majority
original_label: Member States delayed RDE adoption and blocked qualified majority
quote: Several Member States (Italy, Spain, France, the Slovak Republic, Romania and Hungary) prevented the formation of a qualified majority in the TCMV, resulting in a postponement of the vote on the first RDE package, and therefore a delay in the whole RDE process, which is still not completed today, but was initially envisaged to be applicable for compliance purposes as of the date of introduction of the Euro 6 emission limits (2014 for new type approvals and 2015 for all new vehicles).
context: The inquiry documents how Member States used the TCMV voting procedure to delay adoption of real-world emission testing requirements.

label: No enforcement action by Member States until after September 2015
original_label: No enforcement action by Member States until after September 2015
quote: The Member States started to enforce the EU law on emissions from light-duty vehicles as required only after the Volkswagen emissions case broke in September 2015, by conducting additional tests in the laboratory and on the road, and by launching several national investigations into pollutant emissions from passenger cars.
context: The inquiry documents how Member States deferred enforcement action despite having legal obligations, until forced by external events.

label: No penalties imposed on manufacturers despite legal requirement
original_label: No penalties imposed on manufacturers despite legal requirement
quote: Member States have applied neither financial nor legal penalties to car manufacturers in the aftermath of the emissions case. No mandatory initiatives to recall or retrofit non-conform vehicles were taken, and no type-approvals were withdrawn. Where recalls or retrofitting took place, this was done as a voluntary initiative by car manufacturers, following public and political pressure.
context: The inquiry documents the absence of enforcement responses available under existing law, relying instead on voluntary compliance.

label: US EPA Notice of Violation in September 2015 triggered action
original_label: US EPA Notice of Violation in September 2015 triggered action
quote: On 18 September, the EPA issues a Notice of Violation of the Clean Air Act to Volkswagen AG, Audi AG, and Volkswagen Group of America, Inc., alleging that model year 2009-2015 VW and Audi diesel cars (approximately 482000 Golf, Jetta, Passat, Beetle, and Audi A3 cars) equipped with 2-liter diesel engines included illegal defeat device software. Following this event, the Commission and Member States initiated investigations and began enforcement activities.
context: The inquiry identifies an external triggering event that suddenly redirected organizational attention to the emissions issue after years of inaction.

label: Volkswagen scandal prompted national investigations and policy changes
original_label: Volkswagen scandal prompted national investigations and policy changes
quote: After September 2015 Germany, France, the UK, Italy, Spain, Sweden and the Netherlands undertook additional tests beyond the NEDC test, and used the outcomes of these complementary tests to search for the potential use of prohibited defeat devices. In almost all cases the investigating authorities asked the manufacturers for explanations of their emission strategies.
context: The inquiry documents how the Volkswagen disclosure produced a sudden shift in Member State enforcement behavior after years of passivity.

label: European Parliament resolution October 2015 called for investigation
original_label: European Parliament resolution October 2015 called for investigation
quote: On 27 October 2015, the European Parliament adopted a resolution (2015/2865(RSP)) on emission measurements in the automotive sector, condemning 'any fraud by automobile manufacturers' and calling 'for a thorough investigation regarding the role and responsibility of the Commission and of Member State authorities'.
context: The inquiry notes that political attention shifted following the US EPA action, prompting Parliament to establish this investigation committee.

label: TCMV accelerated RDE development after Volkswagen revelations
original_label: TCMV accelerated RDE development after Volkswagen revelations
quote: The work on the second RDE package, setting out the not-to-exceed limits for NOx emissions, started in February 2015 and accelerated after the Volkswagen revelations in September 2015.
context: The inquiry documents how the Volkswagen scandal prompted renewed urgency in regulatory work that had been moving slowly before.

label: Commission launched infringement procedures in December 2016
original_label: Commission launched infringement procedures in December 2016
quote: On 8 December 2016, the Commission initiated infringement procedures against the Czech Republic, Germany, Greece, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Spain and the United Kingdom as regards their provisions on penalties, and against Germany and the United Kingdom for lack of disclosure of technical information on the results of their national investigations.
context: The inquiry documents enforcement action initiated only after the Volkswagen case, despite long-standing legal obligations.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Member States presented public position different from TCMV positions
original_label: Member States presented public position different from TCMV positions
quote: Some Member States presented a different position to the public from that they presented to the participants of the TCMV.
context: The inquiry identifies a gap between what Member States privately advocated in regulatory proceedings and their public statements.

label: No system for exchanging information between technical services
original_label: No system for exchanging information between technical services
quote: Contrary to type-approval authorities, there is currently no specific system in place for exchanging information between technical services, neither is such a system foreseen in the Commission's proposal for reform of EU type-approval.
context: The inquiry identifies an institutional gap in the channels for communicating test results and concerns across the fragmented type-approval system.

label: Technical services chose by manufacturers, minimally audited by authorities
original_label: Technical services chose by manufacturers, minimally audited by authorities
quote: The choice of the technical service is primarily the choice of the car manufacturer, and the role of the type-approval authority is often just to validate the procedure at the end. The possibility available to type-approval authorities to audit technical services and to challenge the choice of technical service is very rarely used.
context: The inquiry documents how decision-making authority was delegated to private actors with financial ties to manufacturers, limiting independent oversight.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: RDE-LDV group agenda dominated by industry reopening settled topics
original_label: RDE-LDV group agenda dominated by industry reopening settled topics
quote: The Commission should have acted to mitigate the central role played by the overrepresented industry representatives in the work of the RDE-LDV working group, who constantly delayed its work by re-opening topics that were considered clarified or even decided upon.
context: The inquiry identifies how the composition of the regulatory working group created an agenda that favored delay and obstruction.

category: Rules of the game and attention-directing incentives
label: Lack of technical expertise in Commission favored industry participation
original_label: Lack of technical expertise in Commission favored industry participation
quote: Over half of the RDE-LDV working group participants consisted of experts from car manufacturers and other automotive industries. This can inter alia be attributed to the lack of sufficient technical expertise in the Commission departments.
context: The inquiry identifies how resource constraints and organizational capability gaps created structural dependence on industry expertise, shaping attention.

label: Commission lacked meaningful and complete minutes of RDE-LDV meetings

context: NHTSA's July 9, 1978 announcement of the initial defect finding, noting Firestone's non-compliance with information requests.

label: NHTSA initial defect determination for Firestone 500 tires
original_label: NHTSA initial defect determination for Firestone 500 tires
quote: The agency says its investigation has clearly established that these tires have failed in significant numbers and that the failures are characterized by blowouts, tread separations, and other failures which have resulted in deaths, injuries, and property damage accidents. The agency believes that these tires still on the highway will continue to fail and that future accidents will occur. Therefore, an initial determination of a safety related defect has been made. The agency believes Firestone Tire and Rubber Co. should immediately issue a recall of these tires.
context: NHTSA's formal finding of a safety defect and recommendation for immediate recall announced July 9, 1978.

label: NHTSA announces public hearing on Firestone defect
original_label: NHTSA announces public hearing on Firestone defect
quote: NHTSA also announced that a public hearing will be held Aug. 7, 1978 at which time Firestone company and any other interested parties, including consumers, will be given the opportunity to present testimony, data, and information relating to this defect finding. After analysis of the data and information presented at the public hearing, NHTSA will then make a final determination. If that final decision upholds the initial safety defect finding, then the agency can order the Firestone company to conduct a recall of the tires.
context: NHTSA's announcement of its procedural response to the Firestone defect finding, setting a public hearing for August 7, 1978.

label: Firestone and DOT agree on massive tire recall
original_label: Firestone and DOT agree on massive tire recall
quote: Some 10-million passenger car tires -- the largest number in history -- will be recalled by the Firestone Tire and Rubber Co. under an agreement announced today by Secretary of Transportation Brock Adams. It is estimated that 7 1/2 million of these tires are still in service. Firestone estimates the recall may cost as much as $230 million.
context: DOT announcement on October 20, 1978 of the settlement agreement between Firestone and NHTSA resulting in recall of 10 million tires.

label: Firestone 500 recall scope and eligibility dates
original_label: Firestone 500 recall scope and eligibility dates
quote: The recalled tires will be replaced free of charge with Firestone 721 Steel Belted Radials, unless the purchaser requests to substitute another Firestone line. The investigation and the settlement were conducted by DOT's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
context: DOT's announcement of recall terms on October 20, 1978.

label: Scope determination based on quality improvements
original_label: Scope determination based on quality improvements
quote: The cutoff dates of May 1, 1976, and Jan. 1, 1977, for the tires being recalled are based on determinations by NHTSA's investigators that after those dates there was an improvement in the quality and performance of the Firestone 500 tires. This was apparently due to changes made in the internal construction of the tires.
context: NHTSA's explanation in the final settlement agreement of October 20, 1978 regarding how the recall scope was determined.

label: Safety belt usage rates and comfort problems
original_label: Safety belt usage rates and comfort problems
quote: Only 14 percent of the nation's drivers use their safety belts, according to a new survey conducted for the U. S. Department of Transportation. A separate study evaluating the comfort and convenience of safety belts in 1979 model cars uncovered a number of problems associated with using these new belt systems.
context: DOT announcement on December 15, 1978 of two research studies on safety belt usage and design problems.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: Light truck sales growth and market dominance
original_label: Light truck sales growth and market dominance
quote: The number of vehicles such as pickup trucks, buses and vans in operation have increased by about 80 percent over the last decade and now account for 89 percent of the truck market. By comparison, the number of passenger cars on the road has increased 32 percent during this period. Sales of these vehicles, half of which are pickup trucks, reached a record 3.4 million units last year, NHTSA said. Ford Motor Co. produced more than 1.1 million of the total, and General Motors 1.4 million.
context: NHTSA statement in November 1978 notice of proposed rulemaking on light truck safety standards, contextualizing the market growth.

label: Light truck fatality rate higher than passenger cars
original_label: Light truck fatality rate higher than passenger cars
quote: NHTSA figures indicate a 25 percent jump in fatalities for this vehicle category between 1975 and 1977, as compared to an increase of only 3.9 percent for passenger cars. In addition, the federal safety agency found that 1975 and 1976 model year light trucks had 21.9 fatalities, against 11.7 fatalities per billion miles for passenger cars of similar weight.
context: NHTSA's analysis in November 1978 rulemaking notice showing higher fatality rates for light trucks compared to passenger cars.

label: NHTSA proposes extension of safety standards to light trucks
original_label: NHTSA proposes extension of safety standards to light trucks
quote: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 201 as amended would require that instrument panels, seat backs, sun visors and arm rests be designed to lessen injuries when persons are thrown against them in crashes. FMVSS No. 203, as applied to light trucks and vans, would require steering assemblies to cushion the impact which occurs when the driver strikes the steering wheel in an accident. FMVSS No. 204 limits the rearward movement of the steering assembly to no more than five inches, when the vehicle crashes into a barrier at 30 miles per hour.
context: NHTSA's proposed amendments to safety standards announced November 28, 1978 to extend protections to light trucks and vans.

label: Motorcycle accident causation analysis
original_label: Motorcycle accident causation analysis
quote: An analysis of detailed data of 900 motorcycle accidents in the last 2 1/2 years in the Los Angeles area shows that 51 percent of the accidents were caused by motorists who said they either did not see the motorcyclist or did not see the rider until it was too late. A motor vehicle turning left into the path of a motorcycle was involved in 45 percent of all accidents.
context: NHTSA announcement on October 31, 1978 of preliminary findings from USC motorcycle accident study showing visibility as major causative factor.

label: Motorcycle helmet effectiveness in reducing head injuries
original_label: Motorcycle helmet effectiveness in reducing head injuries
quote: Interviews with motorcyclists involved in crashes showed that, in their opinion, helmets did not limit their hearing or vision in pre-crash conditions. Clinical evaluation showed that helmets are not responsible for neck or head injuries. An examination of the clinical data also shows the helmet to be the only effective life-saving device in use today.
context: NHTSA announcement on October 31, 1978 reporting preliminary findings from USC study on helmet effectiveness.

label: Helmet law repeal correlates with fatality increase
original_label: Helmet law repeal correlates with fatality increase
quote: In 15 states that repealed their helmet use laws since 1976, and that report whether cyclists involved in accidents were wearing helmets, the number of fatalities involving helmetless cyclists showed a dramatic increase of 88 percent from 1976 to 1977.
context: NHTSA Administrator Claybrook citing evidence on October 31, 1978 of the correlation between helmet law repeal and increased fatalities.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: Traffic fatality rates and speed limit compliance
original_label: Traffic fatality rates and speed limit compliance
quote: The reports note that in the seven years following establishment of a national traffic safety effort in 1966, the fatality rate (the number of deaths per 100 million miles driven) declined steadily from 5.48 to 4.11. Then came the fuel crisis and the permanent imposition of the national 55 miles per hour maximum speed limit in January 1974. The safety effects were dramatic. In 1974, traffic deaths fell by nearly 9,000, from 54,052 to 45,196, and the fatality rate declined from 4.11 to 3.52. The next two years brought little change in the number of deaths on the highway, but there were some further reductions in the fatality rate, despite a fairly substantial growth in the number of miles driven, NHTSA reports.
context: NHTSA analysis in July 1978 annual report to Congress on the effects of the 55 mph speed limit on traffic fatalities.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: Speed creep and rising fatality trend
original_label: Speed creep and rising fatality trend
quote: The 55 mph speed limit proved its value as a fuel economy measure and as a livesaving program. But as average speeds began to inch up and the traffic volume continued to grow, the number of fatalities also went up, NHTSA found.
context: NHTSA's analysis in July 1978 report explaining the rise in traffic fatalities despite prior success of the 55 mph limit.

label: Traffic fatalities rising in 1978
original_label: Traffic fatalities rising in 1978
quote: Traffic fatalities in the United States during the first seven months of the year are running more than 2 percent above the number of deaths recorded for a similar period in 1977, the U. S. Department of Transportation said today. Statistics compiled by the department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) show that the nation's traffic toll for the January-July 1978 period is estimated at 27,000. NHTSA Administrator Joan Claybrook said the figures were particularly distressing and if this trend continues, the death count could reach 50,000 by the end of the year.
context: NHTSA announcement on September 1, 1978 of rising traffic fatality trend for the first seven months of 1978.

label: NHTSA issues consumer advisory on Ford transmission hazard
original_label: NHTSA issues consumer advisory on Ford transmission hazard
quote: The U. S. Department of Transportation issued a Consumer Advisory today warning owners of certain Ford Motor Co. vehicles equipped with automatic transmissions to take precautions when parking their vehicles. The warning came from the department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) which is conducting a formal defect investigation involving certain 1970 through 1978 Ford Motor Co. passenger cars and light trucks.
context: NHTSA consumer advisory issued August 29, 1978 in response to transmission defect investigation.

label: NHTSA recommends precautions for Ford transmission problem
original_label: NHTSA recommends precautions for Ford transmission problem
quote: Precautions to be taken include turning off the engine, pushing the gear selector all the way to the "Park" position and pulling on the selector lever (without raising the lever) to make sure it is secured, and setting the parking brake. Vehicles should never be left unattended with their engines running — not even for the brief period it may take to leave the vehicle to close a garage door, make a pickup at a store or check the mailbox at the end of your driveway.
context: NHTSA's specific recommendations to consumers in its August 29, 1978 advisory about the transmission hazard.

label: NHTSA hotline and reporting procedures for safety problems
original_label: NHTSA hotline and reporting procedures for safety problems
quote: Anyone experiencing this problem is urged to report it to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration; Office of Defect Investigations; 400 Seventh St., SW, Washington, D.C. 20590. The agency's toll-free Auto Safety Hotline (800-424-9393 or in Washington, D.C. metro area 426-0123) can also be used to report this and other safety problems.
context: NHTSA's standard mechanism for receiving consumer reports of safety problems, as shown in multiple press releases throughout 1978.

label: Ford recalls 1978 Fairmonts and Zephyrs for wiper defect
original_label: Ford recalls 1978 Fairmonts and Zephyrs for wiper defect
quote: The Ford Motor Co. is recalling approximately 400,000 of its 1978 Ford Fairmont and Mercury Zephyr vehicles for replacement of the windshield wiper linkage, the U. S. Department of Transportation said today. The department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said it urged Ford to conduct a recall campaign after receiving information concerning windshield wiper failures on these vehicles. A NHTSA letter to the company cited a recent court decision relating to windshield wiper failures on 1971-1973 Mercury Capri vehicles which upheld the agency's finding that windshield wiper failures constitute a safety-related defect.
context: NHTSA announcement on August 11, 1978 of Ford recall based on prior court precedent and NHTSA initiative.

label: Subaru recalls 1978 BRAT for fuel tank defect
original_label: Subaru recalls 1978 BRAT for fuel tank defect
quote: SUBARU OF America, Inc., is recalling 23,000 of its 1978 model BRAT vehicles because of fuel tank leaks, the U.S. Department of Transportation announced today. The company notified the department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), that the fuel tanks on these vehicles may develop hairline cracks. The problem may be caused by a blockage in the fuel evaporative control system which leads to abnormally high pressure in the fuel tank and subsequent stress failure.
context: NHTSA announcement on September 5, 1978 of Subaru's voluntary recall for fuel tank defect.

label: Renault recalls multiple model years for throttle defect
original_label: Renault recalls multiple model years for throttle defect
quote: Renault USA, Inc., will recall more than 28,000 of its 1976, 1977, and 1978 Renault models 5 (Le Car), 12, 15 and 17 vehicles to modify their throttle return systems, the U.S. Department of Transporation announced today. In the case of the Renault model 5 only, the company also will replace the rear turn signal lenses, DOT said. The department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said that as a result of its compliance testing program it determined that certain of these vehicles do not conform to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 124.
context: NHTSA announcement on December 29, 1978 of Renault recall resulting from NHTSA compliance testing.

label: 1978 vehicle and tire recall summary
original_label: 1978 vehicle and tire recall summary
quote: Slightly more than nine million motor vehicles and more than 14.6 million tires were recalled for safety defects in 1978, according to figures released today by the U.S. Department of Transportation. The figures, compiled by the department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, indicate a drop from the record 12.9 million vehicles recalled in 1977, but the 14.5 million tires being recalled by the Firestone Tire and Rubber Co. constitute the largest single tire recall in history.
context: NHTSA's year-end summary released December 29, 1978 of recall activity in 1978.

label: Major automakers' 1978 recall contributions
original_label: Major automakers' 1978 recall contributions
quote: In all, domestic manufacturers recalled 8.1 million vehicles in 199 recall campaigns. Foreign manufacturers recalled 1 million vehicles in 71 campaigns bringing the yearly recall total to 9.1 million cars, trucks, buses and motorcycles. The four major U.S. automakers recalled 7. 7 million of the domestic total. Ford Motor Co. recalled nearly 3.8 million vehicles. General Motors Corp. recalled 1. 7 million vehicles, Chrysler slightly more than 1.5 million vehicles and American Motors 600,000 vehicles.
context: NHTSA's breakdown of recall activity by manufacturer in its year-end 1978 summary.

label: Largest 1978 vehicle recalls
original_label: Largest 1978 vehicle recalls
quote: The largest single vehicle recall in 1978 was conducted by Ford Motor Co. and involved 1.5 million 1971-76 Pinto and Bobcat cars that had potentially unsafe fuel tanks. General Motors recalled 320,000 subcompact Chevettes for a gas tank problem and 265,000 Chevrolet, Pontiac, Oldsmobile and Buick models for defective rear axles. Chrysler Corp. recalled 1.1 million Aspen and Volare models to correct steering defects.
context: NHTSA's identification of the major vehicle recalls in 1978 in its year-end summary.

label: Utah tractor-trailer accident investigation findings
original_label: Utah tractor-trailer accident investigation findings
quote: An accident in August 1977 involving a tractor-trailer that rammed into a passenger car claiming the lives of four teenagers and critically injuring another was not the result of brake failure, according to a report issued today by the U.S. Department of Transportation. The department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), ordered an investigation of the August 18, 1977, accident after the truck driver, who was not hurt, claimed that the brake system on his vehicle failed.
context: NHTSA announcement on September 21, 1978 of accident investigation findings disputing brake failure claim.

label: NHTSA proposes improved driver vision standards
original_label: NHTSA proposes improved driver vision standards
quote: The U.S. Department of Transportation today proposed new standards designed to improve a vehicle driver's field of vision. DOT's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration proposes a new federal standard to provide drivers with an improved direct field of view of their motoring environment. NHTSA's second proposal would amend a current standard -- No. 111 Rearview Mirrors -- to provide drivers with an increased field of view.
context: NHTSA announcement on November 7, 1978 of proposed driver vision standards to reduce blind spots and obstruction.

label: NHTSA launches Ford steering defect investigation
original_label: NHTSA launches Ford steering defect investigation
quote: A suspected safety defect in the steering systems of Ford light trucks and vans produced from 1974 through 1977 is being investigated by the U.S. Department of Transportation. The investigation is being conducted by the department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, and centers on Ford E series Econoline vans and F series light trucks which may suffer steering loss when the steering gear box separates from the frame.
context: NHTSA announcement on December 5, 1978 of investigation into Ford steering defect affecting 1.3 million vehicles.

label: NHTSA receives and analyzes consumer complaints on Firestone tires
original_label: NHTSA receives and analyzes consumer complaints on Firestone tires
quote: The consumer reports analyzed by NHTSA during its investigation included more than 2,200 separate reports alleging more than 7,300 individual tire failures received directly by the agency, those forwarded by consumer groups, and those forwarded by members of Congress on behalf of their constituents. Information provided by Firestone in response to NHTSA inquiries and to Congressman John E. Moss of California in a public hearing held on May 23 was also analyzed by NHTSA.
context: NHTSA's July 9, 1978 announcement describing the evidence collection channels used in the Firestone investigation.

label: Consumers Union criticizes Chrysler Omni/Horizon handling
original_label: Consumers Union criticizes Chrysler Omni/Horizon handling
quote: An evaluation performed by the U. S. Department of Transportation does not show evidence of a safety problem in the stability and handling characteristics of Chrysler's subcompact Dodge Omni and Plymouth Horizon vehicles. That conclusion was announced today by the department's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), whose engineers evaluated the Chrysler cars at two different sites during the last two weeks. The tests were ordered by NHTSA Administrator Joan Claybrook, after Consumers Union, an independent testing organization, announced June 14 that it found the cars to be "unacceptable" because of problems in stability and handling.
context: NHTSA announcement on July 7, 1978 of evaluation results responding to Consumers Union's June 14 criticisms.

label: External expert evaluation contradicts manufacturer claims
original_label: External expert evaluation contradicts manufacturer claims
quote: Three NHTSA engineers and two independent vehicle dynamics experts from the Highway Safety Research Institute (HSRI), University of Michigan, visited Chrysler Corp.'s Chelsea, Mich., Proving Ground to observe and participate in handling and stability tests on Chrysler Omni/Horizon cars and other vehicles. To prevent any possible bias attributable to the particular cars that Chrysler made available for the evaluation, the NHTSA test team rented a Plymouth Horizon and included it in the test sample at Chrysler.
context: NHTSA's methodology in evaluating Chrysler's vehicles to verify the independent testing claims.

label: WVU study finds high on-road NOx emissions
original_label: WVU study finds high on-road NOx emissions
quote: On March 30, 2014, at the 2014 Coordinating Research Council Annual Workshop on Real World Emissions, in San Diego, California, Dr. Marc Besch, of West Virginia University's Center for Alternative Fuels, Engines & Emissions ("WVU") presented the initial results of a study conducted in collaboration with CARB and commissioned by the International Council on Clean Transportation ("ICCT") that found that on-road NOx emissions from two 2.0L VW diesel vehicles (2012 Jetta and 2013 Passat) were significantly higher than the applicable emission standards established by EPA regulations ("ICCT/WVU Study").
context: The complaint describes the public presentation of external research findings showing that VW vehicles emitted far more NOx on the road than EPA standards allowed.

label: Regulatory meetings to discuss AECDs
original_label: Regulatory meetings to discuss AECDs
quote: On October 3 and 5, 2006 respectively, representatives of Volkswagen AG, including [names redacted], representatives of Audi AG, including [names redacted], and senior managers in VWoA's Engineering and Environmental Office ("EEO"), including [names redacted], met first with CARB in El Monte, California, and then with EPA OTAQ in Ann Arbor, Michigan, to discuss the new line of "clean diesel" engines that VW and Audi planned to introduce starting with model year 2009. Both EPA and CARB requested additional information regarding AECDs in the vehicles and asked for follow-up meetings on that topic.
context: The complaint describes formal regulatory notification meetings where VW was expected to disclose auxiliary emission control devices (AECDs) in new vehicles.

label: Formal AECD presentations to EPA and CARB
original_label: Formal AECD presentations to EPA and CARB
quote: On March 19, 2007, representatives of Volkswagen AG, including [names redacted], and representatives of VWoA, including [names redacted], representatives of Audi AG, including [names redacted], met with representatives of EPA in Ann Arbor, Michigan to discuss the engine design of VW's new 2.0L and 3.0L diesel engines and, specifically, the AECDs in those vehicles. Volkswagen AG and Audi AG made presentations to EPA purporting to disclose each of the AECDs in the 2.0L and 3.0L vehicles. On or about March 21, 2007, representatives of Volkswagen AG, including [names redacted], representatives of Audi AG, including [names redacted], and representatives of VWoA, including [names redacted], met with CARB in California to discuss the engine design of VW's new 2.0L and 3.0L diesel engines and, specifically, the AECDs in those vehicles. Volkswagen AG and Audi AG made presentations to CARB purporting to disclose all AECDs in the 2.0L and 3.0L vehicles.
context: The complaint describes scheduled regulatory meetings where VW made formal presentations purporting to disclose all AECDs.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Dual-mode strategy not disclosed to regulators
original_label: Dual-mode strategy not disclosed to regulators
quote: At the March 19, 2007 meeting with EPA, Volkswagen AG, VWoA and Audi AG did not disclose the dual-mode strategies present in the 2.0L and 3.0L vehicles. At the March 21, 2007 meeting with CARB, Volkswagen AG, VWoA and Audi AG did not disclose the dual-mode strategies present in the 2.0L and 3.0L vehicles.
context: The complaint alleges that despite regulatory meetings specifically designed to solicit disclosure of AECDs, VW failed to disclose the defeat device software.

label: Internal testing reveals higher emissions in road mode
original_label: Internal testing reveals higher emissions in road mode
quote: At least as early as 2007, Volkswagen AG was aware that NOx emissions from diesel vehicles intended for sale in the United States that contained the dual-mode strategy emitted NOx at significantly higher levels when the vehicles were in road mode instead of dyno mode.
context: The complaint alleges that VW engineers detected anomalously high emissions in real driving conditions as early as 2007.

label: Warranty claims for emission control system failures
original_label: Warranty claims for emission control system failures
quote: Between 2008 and 2013, as 2.0L Subject Vehicles sold in the United States began to age, they experienced higher rates of warranty claims for parts and components related to emissions control systems.
context: The complaint notes that a pattern of field failures in emission control systems provided another signal of underlying problems.

label: WVU study results circulated internally at Audi and VW
original_label: WVU study results circulated internally at Audi and VW
quote: On or around April 3, 2014, an employee of Audi AG e-mailed a PowerPoint presentation copying several Audi AG, VW AG, and VWoA employees and managers, which shared the reported results of the ICCT/WVU study.
context: The complaint shows that the external research findings were disseminated through internal email within VW companies.

label: Regulatory investigation conducted through twice-monthly calls
original_label: Regulatory investigation conducted through twice-monthly calls
quote: Beginning in or about May 2014 through the present, CARB, in coordination with EPA, has investigated the reasons for the high in-use emissions, repeatedly questioning representatives from VWoA and Volkswagen AG about WVU's findings. Throughout this period, CARB and EPA OTAQ held twice-monthly phone calls during which they discussed certification and compliance matters of mutual concern, including the status of the investigation of the high in-use emissions.
context: The complaint describes the formal regulatory channel through which CARB and EPA coordinated an investigation into the emissions anomalies.

label: VWoA management aware of regulator investigation
original_label: VWoA management aware of regulator investigation
quote: As of May 2014, VWoA management was aware that CARB and EPA were looking into the reasons for the high in-use emissions from the 2.0L diesel vehicles identified by the ICCT/WVU Study.
context: The complaint establishes that VW leadership knew regulators were investigating the emissions problem.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: VW attributes high emissions to technical issues not defeat devices
original_label: VW attributes high emissions to technical issues not defeat devices
quote: On or about May 22, 2014, [names redacted], a certification engineer with Volkswagen AG, and [names redacted], a manager with VWoA's EEO, among other VW representatives, met with CARB representatives at CARB's offices in El Monte, California. At this meeting, Volkswagen AG and VWoA represented that VW believed any higher emissions from its 2.0L diesel engines were attributable to various yet-to-be-identified technical issues with the after-treatment emission control systems and in-use conditions not represented by the FTP.
context: The complaint alleges that when confronted by regulators with the WVU findings, VW responded with alternative explanations that obscured the true cause (the defeat device).

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: VW representatives continue to deny defeat device despite findings
original_label: VW representatives continue to deny defeat device despite findings
quote: On or about October 1, 2014, at a meeting with CARB at its offices in California, representatives of VWoA, including at least [names redacted] and the then-General Manager of VWoA's EEO office, and representatives of Volkswagen AG, including at least [names redacted], acknowledged that VW's internal testing also found higher on-road emissions and represented that the increased emissions from the vehicles studied by WVU/ICCT were attributable to various technical issues with the after-treatment emission control systems and in-use conditions not represented by the FTP.
context: The complaint shows that even after VW's own testing confirmed high emissions, management attributed them to technical issues rather than the software strategy.

label: Powertrain Development division responsible for engine software customization
original_label: Powertrain Development division responsible for engine software customization
quote: Volkswagen AG's Powertrain Development division (sometimes called Engine Development) is responsible for the development of motor vehicle engines, including the customization of ECM software and the development of emission control systems. There are a number of sub-components or departments within Powertrain Development, including Drive Electronics and Diesel Engine Development. Drive Electronics has sub-components that include Function Development (sometimes called Functional/Software Development) and System Application Diesel. Diesel Engine Development also has sub-components that include Ultra-Low Emissions Engines and Exhaust Post-Treatment. Engineers in these groups, among others, work together to develop, customize, and calibrate ECM software for use in diesel engines manufactured by Volkswagen AG and its subsidiaries.
context: The complaint describes the organizational structure and technical divisions responsible for developing and customizing the engine control software containing the defeat device.

label: Akustikfunktion software developed with dual-mode capability
original_label: Akustikfunktion software developed with dual-mode capability
quote: Prior to 2005, engineers at Audi AG developed a software function, which engineers at Volkswagen AG later referred to as the "Akustikfunktion," among other aliases. On or about November 10, 2006, Volkswagen AG's contractor submitted a request, on behalf of Volkswagen AG, for a software design change to the Akustikfunktion for 2.0L diesel engines that created the dual-mode strategy referred to in Paragraphs 88-89.
context: The complaint describes the origination and evolution of the software function that would become the core of the defeat device.

label: Regular internal communications about dual-mode strategy refinements
original_label: Regular internal communications about dual-mode strategy refinements
quote: Between 2006 and 2014, employees in Volkswagen AG's Powertrain Development division, including managers, regularly communicated with each other, and contractors, regarding the design and later refinements of the dual-mode strategy, referred to as the "extended Akustikfunktion," among other aliases.
context: The complaint establishes that knowledge of the dual-mode strategy was distributed across technical teams and managers through regular communications.

label: VW proposes voluntary recall with software update
original_label: VW proposes voluntary recall with software update
quote: At that meeting, and in subsequent meetings on or about November 14, 2014 and December 9, 2014 with CARB, and on or about December 3, 2014 with CARB and EPA, [names redacted], among other representatives of VWoA and Volkswagen AG, proposed that VW conduct a voluntary recall of certain 2.0L Subject Vehicles currently on the road in order to "reflash" or reprogram the EDC17 ECM software to install a new optimized software calibration that would reduce NOx emissions significantly.
context: The complaint describes VW's proposed response to the regulatory questioning: a voluntary recall with software updates rather than disclosure of the defeat device.

label: VW executes voluntary recalls with ECM software updates
original_label: VW executes voluntary recalls with ECM software updates
quote: In December 2014, VWoA issued a voluntary recall for 2.0L Subject Vehicles in the United States that were equipped with an SCR after-treatment system. As part of that recall, new and updated ECM software was installed or "reflashed" in the ECMs of vehicles that had already been sold to customers. In March 2015, VWoA issued a second voluntary recall for 2.0L Subject Vehicles in the United States that were equipped with an LNT after-treatment system. As part of that recall, new and updated ECM software was installed or "reflashed" in the ECMs of vehicles that had already been sold to customers.
context: The complaint documents that VW implemented recalls with software updates, which the complaint later alleges constituted tampering with emission controls after sale to customers.

label: Updated software included steering wheel angle input
original_label: Updated software included steering wheel angle input
quote: In or around 2013, Volkswagen AG engineers developed a software update for the 2.0L Subject Vehicles that contained LNTs (including those that had already been sold to customers) that included the angle of the steering wheel as an additional input to detect when the vehicle was undergoing emission testing. The inclusion of the steering wheel angle input was intended to improve the Akustikfunktion's precision in order to reduce the stress on the emission control systems.
context: The complaint describes an engineering refinement that made the test detection software more sophisticated, suggesting technical expertise directed at avoiding detection.

label: Audi engineers included on change requests for defeat device software
original_label: Audi engineers included on change requests for defeat device software
quote: Engineers at Audi AG were included on, or were listed as contacts for, at least one change request submitted by Volkswagen AG to Bosch for functions related to the dual-mode strategy in the 2.0L Subject Vehicles.
context: The complaint shows that Audi engineers were formally involved in requesting modifications to the defeat device software.

label: Audi engineers responsible for customizing 3.0L ECM software
original_label: Audi engineers responsible for customizing 3.0L ECM software
quote: Engineers at Audi AG were responsible for customizing the EDC17 ECM software used in the 3.0L Subject Vehicles, and communicating with Bosch to develop, test, and calibrate the EDC17 ECM software to be used in those vehicles.
context: The complaint establishes the structural role of Audi engineers in developing the software for the 3.0L vehicles.

label: Audi distributed ECM software files to Porsche for review
original_label: Audi distributed ECM software files to Porsche for review
quote: As early as September 2011, engineers at Audi AG sent engineers at Porsche AG ECM software files that could be reviewed, modified, and calibrated (within the parameters set by the source code) for 3.0L diesel engines intended for use in the United States.
context: The complaint shows that the dual-mode software was shared across companies within the Volkswagen Group for use in different vehicle brands.

label: EPA and CARB request disclosure of AECDs
original_label: EPA and CARB request disclosure of AECDs
quote: Both EPA and CARB requested additional information regarding AECDs in the vehicles and asked for follow-up meetings on that topic.
context: The complaint describes an early regulatory signal that prompted VW to organize formal meetings to address AECD disclosures.

label: VW represents all AECDs disclosed and none are defeat devices
original_label: VW represents all AECDs disclosed and none are defeat devices
quote: On August 3, 2007, VWoA sent EPA a letter referring to the March 19, 2007 meeting and representing (1) that VW had disclosed all AECDs in its "clean diesel" vehicles, and (2) that no AECDs in those vehicles were defeat devices.
context: The complaint shows VW making formal written representations to the EPA after the March meetings, affirming complete disclosure.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: EPA confirmatory testing passes despite undisclosed defeat device
original_label: EPA confirmatory testing passes despite undisclosed defeat device
quote: In 2008, EPA conducted confirmatory testing of certain 2009 Model Year 2.0L and 3.0L Subject Vehicles to confirm compliant emissions from the vehicles using the FTP. The vehicles passed the confirmatory tests. In subsequent years, EPA conducted confirmatory tests on certain Subject Vehicles as new model years and models were introduced. The vehicles passed the confirmatory tests and EPA subsequently certified the vehicles based in large part on these test results, as well as representations made by VW in COC applications and in meetings with EPA OTAQ.
context: The complaint notes that because the defeat device operated in dyno mode during the FTP test procedure, the vehicles appeared compliant even with the hidden software.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: VW engineers seek explanations as investigation progresses
original_label: VW engineers seek explanations as investigation progresses
quote: On or about May 12, 2015, a certification engineer with Volkswagen AG involved in discussions with CARB sent an email to employees at Volkswagen AG, including managers, in response to testing by CARB and exclaimed (in German), "We need a story for the situation!"
english_gloss: "We need a story for the situation!"
context: The complaint quotes an internal email showing that VW engineers recognized the need to develop a narrative to explain the emissions findings to regulators.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: VW engineer expresses concern about CARB testing
original_label: VW engineer expresses concern about CARB testing
quote: On or about June 29, 2015, the same certification engineer again sent an email to other Volkswagen AG employees, with the subject "[C]ARB Status," and stated (in German) "We must be sure to prevent the authority from testing the [2.0L Subject Vehicles that contain LNTs] … If [that vehicle type] goes onto the roller at the CARB, then we'll have nothing more to laugh about!!!!!"
english_gloss: "We must be sure to prevent the authority from testing the [2.0L Subject Vehicles that contain LNTs] … If [that vehicle type] goes onto the roller at the CARB, then we'll have nothing more to laugh about!!!!"
context: The complaint quotes an internal email showing that VW staff sought to limit CARB's ability to test vehicles that would reveal the defeat device.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: VW seeks creative responses to regulator questions
original_label: VW seeks creative responses to regulator questions
quote: On July 2, 2015, the certification engineer sent an email to a number of Volkswagen AG employees with the subject "RE: Status Update USA," seeking input on how to respond to questions from regulators, and noting (in German), "the key word 'creativity' would be helpful here."
english_gloss: "the key word 'creativity' would be helpful here"
context: The complaint quotes an internal email showing management's focus on developing strategically framed responses to regulators.

category: Focus of attention and dominant agendas
label: VW acknowledges lack of good explanations for emissions
original_label: VW acknowledges lack of good explanations for emissions
quote: On or about July 23, 2015, the certification engineer sent a calendar invite to a number of Volkswagen AG employees, with the subject "Status Update" and with an agenda that stated (in German), "[C]ARB is still waiting for Answers . . . . We still have no good explanations!!!!!"
english_gloss: "[C]ARB is still waiting for Answers . . . . We still have no good explanations!!!!!"
context: The complaint quotes an internal communication showing that VW management acknowledged they could not provide explanations that would satisfy regulators.

label: Audi and Porsche informed about CARB off-cycle testing
original_label: Audi and Porsche informed about CARB off-cycle testing
quote: On or around August 26, 2015, an engineer from Audi AG and an engineer with Porsche AG were informed by another Volkswagen AG employee that CARB had used emission test procedures outside of the FTP on the 2.0L Subject Vehicles and CARB had asked what would happen if it ran the same tests on the 3.0L Subject Vehicles.
context: The complaint describes how information about CARB's testing methodology that could expose the 3.0L defeat device was shared among the companies.

label: EPA Notice of Violation issued for 2.0L vehicles
original_label: EPA Notice of Violation issued for 2.0L vehicles
quote: On September 18, 2015, EPA issued a Notice of Violation to Volkswagen AG, VWoA, VWoA Chattanooga, and Audi AG, citing violations of the Act related to the dual-mode strategy in the 2.0L Subject Vehicles.
context: The complaint identifies the regulatory turning point when EPA formally notified VW of the violations.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Document destruction after legal department notification
original_label: Document destruction after legal department notification
quote: In or around late August and September 2015, Volkswagen AG engineers in the Powertrain Development Division purposefully deleted or modified files on their company computers relating to the Subject Vehicles and the dual-mode strategy software after being informed in advance by at least one member of the Volkswagen AG legal department that a litigation hold requiring them to save such documents would be issued.
context: The complaint alleges that after receiving the EPA Notice of Violation, VW employees destroyed evidence of the wrongdoing with advance warning from legal counsel.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: VW continues concealment after Notice of Violation
original_label: VW continues concealment after Notice of Violation
quote: Even after EPA issued the Notice of Violation to Volkswagen AG, Audi AG, and VWoA for the 2.0L Subject Vehicles on September 18, 2015, and after Mr. Horn's testimony before Congress, Audi AG, Volkswagen AG, and VWoA failed to come forward and reveal to regulators that the 3.0L Subject Vehicles contain one or more undisclosed AECDs, including the dual-mode strategy involving the "temperature conditioning mode."
context: The complaint alleges that despite the public exposure of the 2.0L violations, VW continued to conceal the 3.0L defeat device.

label: Audi presents selective on-road emissions data to CARB
original_label: Audi presents selective on-road emissions data to CARB
quote: In response, managers and engineers at Audi AG and VWoA intentionally presented to CARB on-road emission results from the Model Year 2016 3.0L diesel vehicles, and not earlier models, because those test results showed better results than the ICCT/WVU Study.
context: The complaint alleges that VW selectively presented test results to regulators to obscure the existence of the defeat device in 3.0L vehicles.

category: Filtering, discounting and neglect of warnings
label: Audi attributes 3.0L emissions to technical issues
original_label: Audi attributes 3.0L emissions to technical issues
quote: At the March 2015 meeting and in related correspondence with CARB, representatives of Audi AG acknowledged that real world emissions from the 3.0L Subject Vehicles may be three times higher than in test conditions, but ascribed the difference to various technical issues with the after-treatment emission control systems and in-use conditions not represented by the FTP.
context: The complaint shows that even when acknowledging three-fold higher emissions, VW attributed them to technical issues rather than the hidden test-detection software.

label: Porsche and VW circulate ECM software files before detection
original_label: Porsche and VW circulate ECM software files before detection
quote: Between at least March 13, 2015 and April 10, 2015, employees of Porsche AG circulated multiple emails among themselves and with Volkswagen AG's contractor that attached EDC17 ECM software files, including the master software files, for the model year 2016 3.0L Subject Vehicles.
